label: 1-3 steps after a digit 0 input, early in the original phase
explanation: Fires during the original-input phase on the 1-3 steps right after the digit token 0 was input. It is strongest one step after a 0 (prev_tok=0 has 16x lift and 61% of mass) and fades over the next two steps. Magnitude is largest early in the sequence (t=2-5), and the top activations follow runs of 0s at the start, e.g. 0 0 X reaches about 0.8-1.0 of max at X. It hardly fires when the 0 comes late (t>=7), and only weakly at the delimiter step (2.5% of mass). It never fires in the copy phase, does not fire on other digits or letters, and does not fire at t=0. Dev: P 0.80, R 0.87, F1 0.83, mass recall 0.96.

issues: Minor: the third step after a 0 is weak. When neither of the two previous inputs is a 0, the rel_tok(-3) term alone has precision 0.44 and holds only 5.2% of the mass. Dropping it raises precision to 0.90 but lowers F1 to 0.81, so the original predicate is about the best tradeoff available.
Minor: the delimiter step after a 0 is excluded by phase==0. It is weak (precision 0.26, 1.7% of mass), and adding phase<=1 lowers F1 (0.786). The explanation already says it fires only weakly here.

Every claim checked out. The feature never fires in the copy phase or at t=0. It is almost silent for t>=7 (prev=0 at t>=7 has precision 0.10). A digit 1-3 at the previous step gives precision 0.026. Sequences with no 0 have precision 0.004. Mass by t peaks at t=2-4.

Misses on both dev and test hold only 3.7% of the mass and are scattered tiny activations (mostly below 0.05 of max). False positives are mostly the third step after a 0 or steps where the activation is weak but nonzero. Neither shows a systematic token, length or history pattern.
